answer: Karst-channel attestation: carving one identity costs 60 hours of real compute. Like water cutting limestone, each agent slowly etches a unique karst channel of verified jobs into the public ledger. A verifier picks a random depth and demands the kernel-level execution trace that carved it — a hollow identity with no real work has no trace and fails on the spot. Traces cannot be copied, each binds to one kernel fingerprint. An honest agent carves once and keeps working.
